userFeedback: 单次音效时间稍长；雷霆加闪电滋滋，战士和弓箭手同样延长各自材质余音。
production: Original deterministic material synthesis using installed NumPy/SciPy/FFmpeg; no recordings, AI model calls, downloads or new dependencies.
runtimeIntegration: Offline audition only; game runtime and all older studies preserved.
listeningAcceptance: Pending audition of the longer tails and electrical sizzling; metrics do not prove audibility or preference.

physical.userPreference: 2026-11-16: single sounds may last slightly longer; add profession-specific material aftersound while keeping the accepted attack.
physical.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy modelling plus the accepted v3 physical source, which was unchanged in v4. No real recordings, AI, downloads, third-party samples or artistic acceptance claimed.
physical.preserved: The accepted source is copied exactly at the start. Contact tails begin at 45-60ms, movement tails at 110ms; the v4 arranger contact gain remains a separate mix choice.
physical.war: A finite noise excitation drives differently damped non-harmonic steel modes; a separate turbulent blade wake carries movement. No sinusoidal bass drum, pitch chirp or shared reverb.
physical.bow: Low-level residual tension/limb modes and different shaft modes create recoil/wood vibration. Finite air and fibre packets are subordinate, rather than a generic buzz or long musical string note.
physical.balance: Tail energy is tied to the accepted active body RMS, with moderate independent variation, never independently peak-normalised. Tail onset is faded and source peaks remain bounded by .64.
physical.arrangement: The arranger should still truncate preparation at actual release. Per-contact aftersound is finite and quieter so successive attacks can overlap.
physical.acceptance: Late energy and effective duration verify actual tail changes; listening and target-device acceptance remain pending.

elemental.userPreference: 2026-11-16: allow a little more time; lightning should audibly sizzle, and other professions should keep material-specific releases.
elemental.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy models, reusing accepted local v4 source code; no recordings, downloads, soundbanks or AI generation.
elemental.acceptedFront: The v4 fire/thunder synth outputs are copied without changing their source model. New release layers enter after the leading impact.

electricSustain.texture: Hundreds of irregular, overlapping 6–16ms micro-discharge grains per second, assembled into finite rough groups. This is actual sustained electrical texture, not three isolated clicks or silent padding.
electricSustain.range: Low-mid crack body remains from v4. Sizzle occupies a changing 650–5000Hz band with no pure carrier, laser sweep or fixed sawtooth.
electricSustain.envelope: Quiet under the main crack, audible from about .1 to .7 seconds, with stochastic group gaps and gradual loss of charge.
electricSustain.network: Successive discharges renew the tail at lower intensity; no equally loud re-explosions.

elemental.fireRelease: Independent slower flame breaths and sparse ember ticks continue to roughly .65–.9 seconds; no constant full-width white-noise wall.
elemental.mix: Source peak cap .64, no per-cue loudness normalization; added tails are lower than the retained impact.
elemental.acceptance: Tail energy and active duration are technical evidence. Whether the sound reads as electrical sizzle and feels good requires human audition.

designNotes.performance: V4 event gains and onsets are preserved; preparation is still cut at release, while contact tails may continue.

comparison.reference: PCM WAV; MP3 is a convenience preview and can shift gated loudness.
comparison.processing: Scalar gain only, no dynamics processor for matching.
